public_rationale: Capgemini's October–November 2024 survey found shopping-related GenAI satisfaction at 37%, compared with 41% in 2023 [e1]. Applause's February–March 2025 survey reported continuing user problems and fewer hallucination encounters than its previous survey [e2]. The first comparison concerns an earlier period and a particular use; the second measures error encounters rather than a comparable sentiment trend [e1, e2]. Neither establishes whether dissatisfaction increased broadly among GenAI users through March 27, 2025 [e1, e2].
limitations: The satisfaction comparison covers shopping-related use in 2024, not the target period in early 2025 [e1].
Applause's reported error encounters do not establish a representative trend in user dissatisfaction [e2].
The packet lacks broad, comparable repeated sentiment measurements covering the target period [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: User disillusionment with generative AI is continuing to grow.

statement.document_title: GenAI’s day of reckoning may have come

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a broad increase in disappointment or dissatisfaction among people who use generative AI.
An increase in isolated complaints, public anxiety about AI, or the number of users encountering an error does not by itself establish this trend.
Because the statement describes an ongoing state without a dated survey period, the target is the current calendar quarter through March 27, 2025. Earlier observations provide comparison points.
A representative repeated survey is one suitable test; similarly broad and comparable longitudinal user evidence could also qualify.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable measurements show that disappointment or dissatisfaction among generative AI users increased through early 2025, beyond sampling uncertainty and changes in sample composition.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable, sufficiently broad measurements show stable or improving user sentiment over the same period.
